observed_problem.mechanism: Original verify_meta_inputs and verify_meta_engineering load verified inputs independently, re-reading full metadata and source files for SHA256; another action starts a new process without prior in-memory successes.

implementation.scope: Only R1 operational startup context and future owned-stage child bootstrap
implementation.aliases: Canonical definitions and loaded p3work/tools aliases patched by original function object identity; later from-imports inherit canonical wrappers
implementation.entry_evidence: Only successful original native hash calls with stable pre/post file identity; no declared expected SHA seeding
implementation.signature_on_hits: Recheck stat and resolve original argument to detect symlink retarget
implementation.implementation_namespace: Root plus actual native hash implementation file SHA256
implementation.persistence: Operational JSON index, nonblocking file lock, merge latest index, atomic replace
implementation.cache_failure_behavior: Cold original hash; cache write failure does not terminate training
implementation.process_cleanup: Context finally; ordinary atexit and multiprocessing Finalize for owned-stage children
observability: R1_FILE_DIGEST_CACHE_PROGRESS at most once per30seconds on hash calls
implementation.activation: Next new R1 action or owned-stage child; no signal to current warm child

validation.interpreter: Python3.12.14 local stdlib-only optimization, no CUDA execution
meaningful_cases: Real native file_digest and sha256_file return contracts, imported and lazy aliases
Two actual multiprocessing spawn processes: first reads data once, second reads data zero times with same real digest
Same-size content mutation restoring mtime still invalidates ctime; atomic replacement invalidates inode
File mutation during hash never produces a cached entry
Corrupt/unwritable cache degrades to correct native hash; symlink escape uncached
Original validator rejects wrong expected SHA even on cache hit
Failed native read propagates, no entry for impossible returned byte count
Symlink retarget during hit signature causes original hash of new target
Spawned owned child process cache idempotence and normal-exit persistence
Independent process snapshots merge existing entries on flush

limits: First uncached file read still uses the original hash function and may remain slow on school shared storage
Per-trial source QC and direct numpy signal hashing remain native; this does not promise zero validation I/O or second-level startup
A nonblocking flush losing a lock race can lose cache optimization for that exit but not scientific correctness
Real school GPU runtime and filesystem timing have not been measured here
